title: Shelah's Baire-Property Model and Inner-Model Lower Bounds

items.title: Shelah sweetness models for forcing

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Use the library convention that q≤p means q is stronger. A Shelah sweetness model is a tuple (P,D,(E_n) for n<ω) where P is a forcing preorder, D is dense, each E_n is an equivalence relation on D with countably many classes, E_(n+1) refines E_n, and every E_n-class is downward directed. If p_i∈D for i≤ω and p_i E_i p_ω for every i<ω, then the sequence has a common lower bound; moreover, for every n the tail {p_i:n≤i≤ω} has a common lower bound in the E_n-class of p_ω. Finally, for every p,q∈D and n there is k such that, for every p' E_k p, if some r E_n q satisfies r≤p, then some r' E_n q satisfies r'≤p'. A sweetness model M_2 extends M_1 exactly when P_1 is a complete suborder of P_2, D_1⊆D_2, each old E_n is the restriction of the new one, every new E_n-class meeting D_1 is contained in D_1, and if q∈D_1, p∈D_2 and q≤p then p∈D_1. Boolean-algebra language means the corresponding separative completion.
items.proof_plan: Translate Shelah Definitions 7.2 and 7.9 once and for all from the paper's larger-is-stronger order to the library's smaller-is-stronger order. In particular, source upper bounds become library lower bounds. Verify that the displayed conditional transfer clause is exactly source 7.2(d). Also prove the frequently used comparable reformulation: if q≤p, then for every n some k makes each p' E_k p have a common strengthening q' E_n q with q'≤q,p'; conversely, apply that comparable case to the source clause's witness r E_n q to recover the full conditional form. Passing to the separative quotient and regular-open completion preserves compatibility, density, complete embeddings and generic extensions, so all later preorder and Boolean presentations are typed consistently.
items.axiom_base: ZF; no choice principle is used in the definition

items.title: Sweet forcings are sigma-directed and ccc

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: If (P,D,(E_n)) is a sweetness model, then D, and hence P, is a countable union of directed subsets. Consequently every antichain in P is countable, so P satisfies the countable chain condition.
items.proof_plan: Fix n=0. The countably many E_0-classes cover D, and each is directed by the definition. A dense subset that is a countable union of directed sets transfers that decomposition to compatibility witnesses in P. An antichain meets the upward compatibility cone generated by each class in at most one member: two members assigned to one class have extensions into D and then a common extension inside that directed class. Map the antichain injectively into the countable class index. This proves ccc without selecting a representative from every class.
items.axiom_base: ZF; countability is supplied as part of the sweetness witness

items.title: Sweet density transfers along complete suborders

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Let P be a complete suborder of BA(Q), let (Q,D,(E_n)) be sweet, and let (A_j)_(j<ω) be subsets of P whose union is dense. Suppose q∈D and p∈P forces q∈Q/P. Then some j,k have the following uniform property: for every q' E_k q there is p'∈A_j with p'≤p which forces q'∈Q/P. Moreover, the union of all A_j for which such a k exists is dense below p. This is the full two-part conclusion of Shelah Claim 7.4, in the library order.
items.proof_plan: Repeat every j infinitely often as j(i). If no uniform pair existed, recursively choose q_i E_i q which is bad for A_(j(i)). The sequential sweetness clause gives a diagonal lower bound q* in the required tail classes. Apply the transfer clause to a common strengthening of p and q to ensure q* is compatible with p, then use completeness to choose p'≤p forcing q*∈Q/P. Meet the dense union in some A_j. At a later occurrence j(i)=j beyond the transfer modulus, the same p' forces q_i∈Q/P, contradicting its choice. Repeating the argument below each p_0≤p proves density of the union of the good A_j. The recursive bad-witness construction is performed under DC; no stronger choice is used.
items.axiom_base: ZF+DC; DC supplies the recursive bad-witness sequence in Claim 7.4

items.title: Shelah amalgamation preserves sweetness

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Let Q_1 and Q_2 be sweet forcings and let P_0 be completely embedded in BA(Q_1) and BA(Q_2). Their Boolean amalgam Q_1*_(P_0)Q_2 is sweet and contains complete canonical copies of Q_1 and Q_2. If the sweetness model on Q_2 extends a fixed model on Q_1 in the sense of Definition 7.9, the amalgam can be equipped with a sweetness model extending that fixed model. The formulation also permits two named complete embeddings of P_0, by identifying their images before taking the amalgam.
items.proof_plan: Use pairs (q_1,q_2) simultaneously admitted by one P_0-condition as the dense presentation. Decompose a dense subset of P_0 into countably many pairwise compatible sets A_j. Apply the full uniform conclusion of Claim 7.4 first to Q_1 and then to Q_2; this yields, for every pair, a least common modulus m such that all sufficiently equivalent coordinate pairs have compatible P_0-reductions in one A_j. Define the nth amalgam equivalence relation by the two old E_(m+n)-classes together with equality of m. The uniform modulus proves directedness, the sequential bound and transfer clauses; it is not replaceable by ordinary predensity. Verify both canonical embeddings by reductions. For the extension form, adjoin the old dense set and use the exact restriction clauses of Definition 7.9, as in Claim 7.12. Sweetness then gives ccc.
items.axiom_base: ZF+DC through the full Claim 7.4 supplier

items.title: Shelah's universal-meagre forcing

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: The universal-meagre forcing UM consists of pairs (t,T), where T is a perfect nowhere-dense subtree of 2^(<ω) and t=T∩2^(≤n) is its finite initial tree through some height n. In the library order, (t_2,T_2)≤(t_1,T_1) exactly when T_1⊆T_2 and t_1 is the restriction of t_2 through the old height. Thus stronger conditions enlarge the witness tree while permanently preserving the recorded finite initial tree. The generic union of the finite initial trees is a perfect nowhere-dense tree U_G. The meagre envelope of the old nowhere-dense sets is a countable union of finite-prefix rearrangements of [U_G], not [U_G] alone.
items.proof_plan: Spell out finite tree restriction, perfection, nowhere density and the agreement clause, translating Definition 7.7 from Shelah's order to the library order. Reflexivity and transitivity follow because successive initial-tree agreement composes and witness-tree inclusion is transitive. Compatible conditions have a common extension obtained from the finite union of their witness trees; that union remains perfect and nowhere dense and respects the longer recorded initial tree. Dense height extensions make U_G closed and nowhere dense: once an omitted extension is recorded below the finite height, no stronger condition can add it. Do not claim that one arbitrary old tree is directly included in U_G; Claim 7.15 uses the countable family of prefix rearrangements built in the next lemma.
items.axiom_base: ZF

items.title: A universal-meagre generic absorbs old nowhere-dense sets

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Forcing with UM makes the union of all ground-model closed nowhere-dense subsets of Cantor space meagre. Therefore every ground-model meagre set is contained in one meagre set coded by the UM generic.
items.proof_plan: Let U_G be the generic perfect nowhere-dense tree. Enumerate the countable set of finite prefix rearrangements π of the binary tree, and put M_G equal to the union of the closed nowhere-dense sets [π(U_G)]. For a fixed old nowhere-dense tree S and condition, the standard finite-tree surgery from Definition 7.7 is dense: at a later height, attach each finitely many surviving S-sections to a distinct section of the enlarged witness tree and record the finite prefix rearrangements used. The resulting condition forces [S] into a finite subunion of M_G. Genericity meets this dense set separately for every old S, so the union of all old closed nowhere-dense interpretations is contained in the one countable F-sigma meagre set M_G; no enumeration of the ground-model trees is used. An old countable closed-nowhere-dense cover of each old meagre set proves the second assertion. This is the finite-prefix-rearrangement proof implicit in Shelah Claim 7.15, not the false assertion that [S]⊆[U_G].
items.axiom_base: ZF in the forcing argument; no enumeration of all ground-model nowhere-dense sets is used

items.title: Composition with universal-meagre forcing preserves sweetness

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
references.locator: Composition Lemma 7.6, Definition 7.7, Subclaim 7.8, and Claim 7.11, pp. 36-40

items.statement: If P has a sweetness model and P forces that Q is UM, then the two-step iteration P*Q has a sweetness model extending that of P. This remains true in the strengthened extension-of-models form used at successor stages.
items.proof_plan: Use the dense set of pairs (p,(t,T)) with p in the old sweet dense set. Enumerate all old equivalence classes A_m. Define E_n by equality of t, sufficiently fine old E-relations, agreement on which A_m reduce p, agreement on the Boolean decisions that a finite string lies in T, and equality of the finitely many transfer moduli k_m(p). Subclaim 7.8 gives stability under a fine equivalent strengthening. Verify equivalence/countably many classes; directedness by unioning the two tree names over a common old bound; sequential common lower bounds by unioning the tree names and proving the union forced nowhere dense via the diagonal avoidance construction; and the transfer clause by synchronizing the finitely many k_m. Finally verify exact restriction to P. This is the complete Claim 7.6 proof route, not an appeal to generic finite-support preservation.
items.axiom_base: ZF+DC; the source proof uses countable quotient-class enumerations and recursive witness choices

items.title: Continuous countable unions of sweetness models remain sweet

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Let (P_i,D_i,(E_n^i)) for i<δ be a continuous increasing chain of sweetness models, where δ has countable cofinality and every successor extends its predecessor in the exact sweetness-model sense. Then the direct union forcing, dense set, and stabilized equivalence relations form a sweetness model, and every P_i is a complete subforcing of the union.
items.proof_plan: Choose a fixed increasing cofinal sequence in the given countable-cofinality ordinal δ and replace the chain by that subsequence. Put D equal to the union of the D_i. The exact restriction clauses make E_n independent of the stage containing both arguments. Countable classes follow from a countable union of countable class indices. Directedness occurs in a common later stage. For a sequence eventually E_n-equivalent for every n, recursively choose stages containing its initial data and use the extension transfer moduli to diagonalize; the sequential-bound clause at the union is witnessed at the limit of those stages. Completeness follows because every maximal antichain of an earlier stage remains predense at each later stage and hence in the union.
items.axiom_base: ZF+DC; CC counts the union of the stagewise quotient classes and DC supplies the diagonal witness recursion

items.title: Sweet amalgamation extends partial Boolean isomorphisms

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Let B_0 and B_1 be countably generated complete subalgebras of a sweet complete Boolean algebra B, and let h:B_0→B_1 be a complete Boolean isomorphism. There is a sweet complete Boolean algebra B* containing B completely in which h extends to an automorphism of B*. The extension may be chosen compatibly with any previously fixed sweetness-model embedding.
items.proof_plan: Start with two copies of B amalgamated over h. Alternately amalgamate the current algebra with its two images so that the partial map acquires a forward and an inverse extension. At each finite stage apply the sweet amalgamation theorem and track the canonical complete embeddings. At the omega limit use the continuous-union lemma. The union of the coherent partial maps is total, its inverse is the union of the inverse maps, and preservation of complements, arbitrary joins from each stage, and the complete embedding of B follow stagewise. This verifies automorphism rather than merely an injective endomorphism.
items.axiom_base: ZF+DC; the omega back-and-forth is a dependent recursive construction

items.title: Shelah's CH-length homogeneous sweet construction

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Assume ZFC and CH, explicitly |P(omega)|=aleph_1. There is a continuous chain (B_α) for α<ω_1 of sweet complete Boolean algebras of size at most ω_1 whose union B is ccc and has size ω_1, such that every isomorphism between countably generated complete subalgebras that appears at a stage extends to an automorphism at a later stage, every required free-amalgamation task is met, and above every stage there is a later quotient forcing equivalent to UM. This is Shelah's continuous sweet construction; it is not identified with an ordinary finite-support iteration.
items.proof_plan: Under AC and CH, well-order all stage data of hereditary size at most ω_1: names for countably generated complete subalgebras, their isomorphisms, free-amalgamation requests, and UM requests. Use an ω_1 bookkeeping map that repeats every task cofinally often. At an isomorphism stage apply the preceding extension theorem; at a UM stage apply the composition theorem; at limit ordinals use the continuous-union lemma (limits below ω_1 are countable). Induction preserves size at most ω_1 and complete embeddings. The final union is ccc by sweetness/sigma-directedness, and boundedness of countable task codes ensures every genuine task occurs at some stage and is later met. AC is used exactly to well-order the task set and choose the recursive construction; CH bounds it by ω_1.
items.axiom_base: ZFC+CH; full AC is used for the global bookkeeping well-order and transfinite recursive choices

items.title: Real names are captured and coded meagre unions are absorbed

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: In the generic extension by the final algebra B, every name for a real, a Borel code, or a countable sequence of ordinals is equivalent to a name over some B_α. Consequently, for every such sequence s, a later UM quotient makes the union of all meagre Borel sets coded in V[s] meagre. When the construction starts over L, the choices made by the generic on the countably many deciding antichains for s are coded by one real, while the ground-model name and antichain enumerations have ordinal codes; hence s is definable from that real and finitely many ordinals.
items.proof_plan: For each coordinate of a real, Borel code, or ordinal-sequence name, take a deciding maximal antichain. The ccc makes it countable. Ambient AC makes the countable union of these antichains countable; its stage set is bounded in ω_1, so completeness makes the object a B_α-name. Over L, enumerate each deciding antichain canonically and let one real record the unique index met by the generic at every coordinate. An ordinal codes the ground-model name together with these enumerations, so valuation defines s from that real and ordinal; no claim that an ultrafilter on an arbitrary countably generated complete algebra is determined by its generators is needed. Now choose one later stage β whose quotient is UM. Since V[s]⊆V[G_α], every closed nowhere-dense code in V[s] is old at stage β; Claim 7.15 absorbs all of them into one generic meagre F-sigma envelope. Replacing each meagre Borel code by its countable closed-nowhere-dense cover proves the stated union meagre. No ω_1-long stage-by-stage union is asserted.
items.axiom_base: ZFC in the ambient forcing extension; regularity of ω_1 and the ccc name calculation are explicit

items.title: Strongly homogeneous truth has Baire representatives

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Robert M. Solovay, A Model of Set-Theory in Which Every Set of Reals Is Lebesgue Measurable

items.statement: Let B be the final Boolean algebra of the Shelah construction. For every formula φ(x,s,γ⃗) with a countable ordinal-sequence parameter s and finitely many ordinal parameters γ⃗, the set of reals x for which the B-generic extension satisfies φ(x,s,γ⃗) differs from a Borel set by a meagre set. In particular this holds for real-and-ordinal parameters. The Borel code and meagre-error code belong to the final extension.
items.proof_plan: Capture the name for s in a countably generated complete subalgebra B_0. For the Cohen algebra C over B_0, compare any two complete embeddings of B_0*C into B which agree on B_0. The free-amalgamation clause of the CH construction embeds their ranges freely over B_0, and the partial-isomorphism clause extends the induced map to an automorphism of B. Thus the Boolean truth value of φ(c,s,γ⃗), for the canonical Cohen name c, depends only on a finite Cohen condition. The union of basic cylinders whose conditions force φ gives an open set U; reals on which neither side is locally forced lie in the union of the Borel meagre sets coded over V[s]. The preceding one-stage UM absorption theorem makes that entire error set meagre. Every real outside it is Cohen generic over the captured parameter model and is carried to the canonical name by the extended automorphisms, so membership agrees with U. This is the countable-sequence specialization of Solovay's category argument, using the displayed Shelah free-amalgamation, automorphism and absorption hypotheses. Borel-code absoluteness transfers U and the error witness to the inner model.
items.axiom_base: ZFC in the ambient extension; the conclusion is a statement later internalized in ZF+DC

items.title: The Shelah HOD(S) model and its real-ordinal presentation

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Robert M. Solovay, A Model of Set-Theory in Which Every Set of Reals Is Lebesgue Measurable

items.statement: For the inner-model branch, start the CH construction over the constructible ground L. In the generic extension let S be the class of all countable sequences of ordinals and define N=HOD(S): every member of the transitive closure is uniquely definable in a rank from one s∈S and finitely many ordinals. Finite and countable lists of S-parameters interleave into one, and every real belongs to N. By the preceding countably-generated-support coding over L, this is precisely the convenient HOD(S) presentation of the hereditary real-and-ordinal model required by Shelah 7.17: every set of reals in N is definable from one real and finitely many ordinals. No equality with L(R), HOD(R), or any class built from all ω_1-sequences is asserted.
items.proof_plan: Rank-bounded satisfaction makes OD(S) and HOD(S) first-order. A fixed pairing on ω interleaves countably many countable ordinal sequences, and a real is itself such a sequence. For the real-and-ordinal presentation, take the B-name for the one S-parameter defining A⊆R. The capture lemma supplies countably many canonically enumerated deciding antichains; one real records the generic's chosen index in each, and V=L gives an ordinal code for the ground-model name and enumerations. Substitute the resulting definition of s into the rank-bounded definition of A. Conversely, a real plus finitely many ordinals interleaves into one member of S. This proves the advertised equivalence in the only branch where it is used and does not claim that an arbitrary countable ordinal sequence is intrinsically real-coded in an arbitrary ground extension.
items.axiom_base: ZF for the class definition

items.title: The Shelah inner model is closed under ambient omega-sequences

references.title: Robert M. Solovay, A Model of Set-Theory in Which Every Set of Reals Is Lebesgue Measurable

items.statement: If f belongs to the ambient ZFC forcing extension and maps omega into N=HOD(S), then f itself belongs to N.
items.proof_plan: Formula, rank, finite-ordinal and S-parameter codes give a definable surjection Ord×S onto N. Ambient AC is used exactly once to choose for every n a code (α_n,s_n) for f(n). Interleave the sequence of s_n and the ordinal-code sequence α_n into one member of S. The graph of f is then definable from that S-parameter, and heredity follows because every value lies in N. This is the published Solovay closure proof verbatim at the HOD(S) interface; it uses neither UM nor a claim that an ordinal sequence is a real.
items.axiom_base: Ambient ZFC; AC is used only for simultaneous selection of definition codes

items.title: The Shelah inner model satisfies ZF and Dependent Choice

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Robert M. Solovay, A Model of Set-Theory in Which Every Set of Reals Is Lebesgue Measurable

items.statement: N=HOD(S) is a transitive inner model with the same ordinals and reals as the ambient Shelah extension, satisfies every axiom of ZF, and satisfies the serial-relation form of Dependent Choice.
items.proof_plan: Transitivity, all ordinals, all reals, Extensionality, Foundation, Pairing, Union and Infinity are immediate from hereditary definability. Prove Separation by conjoining fixed definitions; Replacement by defining the image from fixed codes for the function and domain, without selecting a code per value; and Power Set by the uniform OD(S) predicate. For DC, take in N a nonempty A, serial R on A, and a_0. Ambient AC recursively produces an R-chain. The closure lemma puts that omega-sequence in N, and transitivity makes the relation computations absolute. This copies the audited Solovay inner-model proof only at its general HOD(S) interface.
items.axiom_base: The inner conclusion is ZF+DC; ambient ZFC supplies the sequence later internalized by omega-closure

items.title: Every real set in the Shelah inner model has the Baire property

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Robert M. Solovay, A Model of Set-Theory in Which Every Set of Reals Is Lebesgue Measurable
references.locator: Part III, Sections 1.6 and 2.8-2.10, pp. 42 and 52

items.statement: N satisfies: every subset of the reals has the property of Baire. Explicitly, for each A in N there are in N an open set U and a meagre set M such that A is the symmetric difference of U and a subset of M.
items.proof_plan: A set A of reals in N has a rank-bounded definition from one s∈S and finitely many ordinals. Apply the preceding homogeneity theorem, whose statement now includes exactly that S-parameter, to obtain an open/Borel approximation C and a coded meagre error. Their codes and the countable nowhere-dense witness sequence are countable objects, hence belong to N by omega-closure; absoluteness gives the same interpretations in N. Convert a Borel approximation to an open one modulo a coded meagre set and interleave the two error witnesses. Then N itself verifies the symmetric-difference inclusion. No result from the published Recorded Shelah remark is consumed.
items.axiom_base: ZF+DC inside N

items.title: The exact equiconsistency of ZFC and the all-Baire-property model

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: The following theories are equiconsistent: ZFC; ZFC plus every real set first-order definable from a real and ordinal parameter has the Baire property; and ZF+DC plus every set of reals has the Baire property. In particular, Con(ZFC) is equivalent to Con(ZF+DC+all real sets have BP), with no inaccessible-cardinal hypothesis.
items.proof_plan: Forward: from a model/finite-fragment witness for ZFC pass to its constructible inner model, which satisfies ZFC+GCH and hence CH. Apply the uniformly definable Shelah forcing and the formal forcing-transfer compiler; the preceding construction gives the real/ordinal-definable BP clause in the full extension and the HOD(S) inner model gives ZF+DC+all BP. Spell this fragment by fragment so a transitive-model assumption is not substituted for Con(ZFC). Reverse: any model of either stronger theory has an internal constructible universe; the constructible semantic/formal schema and its definable well-order yield a model/finite-fragment witness for ZFC. BP plays no role in the reverse implication.
items.axiom_base: Metatheory of formal relative consistency; object-theory conclusions exactly as stated

items.title: Boldface Sigma-one-three measurability

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: For a real parameter x, a subset A of Baire or Cantor space is Sigma^1_3(x) when membership has the form: there exists a real y, for every real z, there exists a real w such that an arithmetic predicate of the displayed reals, x, and a natural-number code holds. Boldface Sigma^1_3 measurability means that every Sigma^1_3(x) set is Lebesgue measurable for every real x. Sigma^1_2(x) sets are included by a dummy final existential quantifier.
items.proof_plan: Define arithmetic predicates using natural-number quantification and fixed real coding. Use the published Cantor/Baire coding maps to show that changing between the two sequence spaces preserves the pointclass and transports completed coin measure to Lebesgue measurability. Verify closure under adding dummy real quantifiers, which is the exact implication used later from Sigma^1_3 measurability to Sigma^1_2 measurability.
items.axiom_base: ZF; this is a coding definition

items.title: Rapid filters and the Raisonnier family

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: A filter F on omega is rapid when it extends the Frechet filter and, for every increasing f:omega→omega, some a∈F satisfies |a∩f(n)|≤n for every n. Equivalently, it is enough that one fixed strictly increasing g uniformly replace n on the right for every increasing f; the Frechet filter then permits deletion of one finite initial segment to recover the exact inequality. For distinct binary reals u,v let h(u,v) be their first differing coordinate and H(X)={h(u,v):u,v∈X,u≠v}. For a real x, a∈F(x) exactly when a countable cover (F_n) of L[x]∩2^omega satisfies the union of all H(F_n) is contained in a.
items.proof_plan: Prove Ishii Lemma 3.6 explicitly. The forward direction takes g(n)=n. Conversely apply the uniform-g hypothesis to f*(n)=f(g(n+1)); on each interval [g(n),g(n+1)) obtain the desired bound after deleting the finite set f(g(0)), which preserves filter membership because the Frechet filter is contained in F. Check that first difference exists and that H is invariant under closure by approximating two distinct closure points through their first-difference coordinate. Thus witnessing cover members may be replaced by closed tree bodies. The filter and rapidity assertions are still proved separately from the definition.
items.axiom_base: ZF

items.title: The Raisonnier family is a Sigma-one-three filter

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice and omega_1^{L[x]}=omega_1. Then F(x) is a proper filter on omega extending the Frechet filter, and membership a∈F(x) is a Sigma^1_3(x) property of the real a.
items.proof_plan: Upward closure is immediate. For a,b, intersect their two countable covers using a fixed pairing of omega; first differences in an intersection lie in both a and b. To exclude the empty set, GCH in L[x] gives omega_1 many constructible reals; regularity of omega_1 from CC implies one member of any countable cover is uncountable and therefore has two distinct elements. The cylinder cover by strings of length n witnesses every cofinite tail. For complexity, replace cover members by closed tree bodies using H(cl F)=H(F), code the tree sequence by one real, and write coverage of L[x] reals plus the first-difference inclusion as a Pi^1_2(x) matrix using the canonical definability of L[x]. Its existential tree-code prefix is Sigma^1_3(x).
items.axiom_base: ZF+Countable Choice; CC is used exactly for regularity of omega_1 and the countable-cover argument

items.title: Rapid filters are not Lebesgue measurable

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: Every rapid filter on omega, regarded through characteristic functions as a subset of Cantor space with coin measure (and hence through the standard coding as a real set), is not Lebesgue measurable.
items.proof_plan: A measurable filter extending the Frechet filter is invariant under finite changes. The complement map sends it to a disjoint set of equal measure, so the standard tail/Sierpinski argument makes the filter null. To contradict nullity, show it meets every closed positive set B. Recursively choose finite antichains T_i at increasing levels so B is almost covered by their cylinders and every conditional B-density above a node of T_i exceeds 1-2^{-(i+2)}; choose them canonically using the density theorem. Rapidity supplies a in F sparse at the level bounds n_i. Inductively choose nested s_i in T_i and points of B satisfying value 1 on the sparse coordinates: independence gives measure above 2^{-(n_i+i+2)}, larger than the uncovered error. The union b lies in closed B and contains a modulo finitely many points, hence b∈F. Thus F meets every closed positive set and has positive outer measure, contradicting nullity.
items.axiom_base: ZF+Countable Choice; CC is declared directly because the published Lebesgue density theorem consumes it

items.title: A measurable null-code order bounds the constructible null union

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: For a real x define A(x) on pairs (u,v) by comparing the least canonical L[x] null G-delta codes containing u and v. Then A(x) is Sigma^1_2(x). Under Countable Choice, if A(x) is measurable, the union G of all null Borel sets coded in L[x] is null in the ambient universe.
items.proof_plan: Enumerate the canonical L[x] null G-delta codes by increasing constructible rank/order and disjointify their interpretations as G_tilde_ξ. Then A(x) is exactly the set of pairs whose unique first-code indices satisfy ξ(u)<ξ(v), making the Sigma^1_2 definition explicit. Every vertical section is an initial union of fewer than omega_1 coded null sets; CC makes omega_1 regular, so this is a countable union and null. Fubini says almost every horizontal section is null. If every horizontal section indexed by u in G is nonnull, the exceptional-index set forces G null; otherwise choose an index with null horizontal section and decompose G into its null initial part, its one null layer, and that null horizontal tail. Outer regularity upgrades the calculation to the completed measure. Thus G is null.
items.axiom_base: ZF+Countable Choice; CC is used for omega_1 regularity/countability of initial code segments, and completed Fubini is used exactly once

items.title: Uniform null G-delta sets capture block functions

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: There are uniformly assigned null G-delta sets N_f in Cantor space for f in omega^omega and, for each open U of measure below one, finite capture sets φ_U(n) of size at most 2^(n+1), such that N_f⊆U implies f(n)∈φ_U(n) for all sufficiently large n. If f belongs to a transitive model, the code for N_f belongs to that model.
items.proof_plan: Use independent coordinate blocks B_(n,m), each of measure 2^{-(n+1)}, and set N_f to the intersection over k of the union over n≥k of B_(n,f(n)); the tail-union estimate makes it null G-delta and its code is uniform in f. For K=2^omega minus U, remove the countably many null basic pieces and let A_s(n) list those m for which K∩[s] misses B_(n,m). Coordinate independence shows the series sum_n |A_s(n)|/2^{n+1} converges; choose the least threshold n(s), then unite A_s(n) over canonically indexed s with n(s)≤n to obtain |φ_U(n)|≤2^{n+1}. If N_f⊆U, the closed Baire space K cannot meet every tail union densely; a basic piece [s] and tail k missed by K force f(n)∈A_s(n)⊆φ_U(n) eventually. Every choice is least in a fixed countable order.
items.axiom_base: ZF; canonical least choices and the complete-metric Baire theorem avoid an unstated choice principle

items.title: Null-code measurability makes the Raisonnier filter rapid

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: Assume Countable Choice, omega_1^{L[x]}=omega_1, and measurability of the Sigma^1_2(x) null-code order A(x). Then the Raisonnier filter F(x) is rapid.
items.proof_plan: Given increasing block endpoints n_i and f∈L[x]∩2^omega, apply the uniform lemma to the coded block-prefix function i↦f restricted to n_i, obtaining an L[x]-coded null G-delta. The null-code lemma makes the union of all these sets null; cover it by one open U of measure below one. Hence every constructible f is eventually captured by φ_U(i). Put into a the first-difference coordinates in block i realized by two length-n_i strings coded in φ_U(i). Partition the constructible reals by a finite initial string after which all prefixes are captured; these countably many classes witness a∈F(x). For a finite family X of equal-length binary strings, the set of first splitting levels H(X) has size at most |X|-1: compress X to its finite prefix tree and inject each realized first-difference level into a distinct branching node below a leaf. Hence |a∩(n_(i-1),n_i]|≤|φ_U(i)|≤2^{i+1}, and summing gives |a∩n_i|≤2^{i+2}-2. Apply the uniform-bound equivalence proved with the rapid-filter definition, then delete the finite initial part, to obtain exact rapidity.
items.axiom_base: ZF+Countable Choice; CC enters through the two preceding filter/null-code lemmas

items.title: Failure of inaccessibility in L produces a real with correct omega-one

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: Work in ZF+Countable Choice. If the ambient omega_1 is not an inaccessible cardinal of L, then there is a real x such that omega_1^{L[x]} equals the ambient omega_1.
items.proof_plan: Countable Choice makes ambient omega_1 regular. It is a cardinal in L, since an L surjection from a smaller ordinal would remain a surjection in the universe; it is regular in L, since an L cofinal map would remain cofinal. If it is not inaccessible in L, GCH in L therefore makes it α^+ in L for some α<omega_1. The ordinal α is countable in the universe, so choose one real coding a bijection omega→α and let x be that code. In L[x], α and every smaller L-cardinal are countable, hence every β<omega_1 is countable. Conversely omega_1 cannot become countable in the inner model L[x], because a witnessing real/function would also exist in the universe. Thus omega_1^{L[x]}=omega_1. Only this existential x is retained; no theorem for every L[r] is stated.
items.axiom_base: ZF+Countable Choice; CC supplies regularity of ambient omega_1 and the enumeration of the countable α

items.title: Sigma-one-three measurability makes omega-one inaccessible in L

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals
references.locator: Theorems 3.3-3.4 and their proofs, pp. 43 and 50-51

items.statement: Assume ZF+Countable Choice and boldface Sigma^1_3 measurability. Then the ambient omega_1 is an inaccessible cardinal in L.
items.proof_plan: Suppose not. The preceding lemma gives a real x with omega_1^{L[x]}=omega_1. Sigma^1_3 measurability includes Sigma^1_2(x) measurability, so the null-code order A(x) is measurable. The Raisonnier theorem makes F(x) a rapid filter, while its complexity lemma makes it Sigma^1_3(x). Mokobodzki's theorem says every rapid filter is nonmeasurable, contradicting the hypothesis. Therefore omega_1 is inaccessible in L. This proof uses no Recorded result and states only the binding L conclusion, although the consulted secondary treatment proves a stronger theorem.
items.axiom_base: ZF+Countable Choice; no full AC

items.title: All-real-set measurability yields an inaccessible inner model

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: If a universe satisfies ZF+DC and every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable, then its constructible universe L satisfies ZFC and contains an inaccessible cardinal—indeed the ambient omega_1 is inaccessible in L. Consequently this theory has at least the consistency strength of ZFC plus an inaccessible cardinal.
items.proof_plan: DC implies Countable Choice by the published implication theorem. Universal measurability implies boldface Sigma^1_3 measurability, so the exact lower-bound theorem makes ambient omega_1 inaccessible in L. The constructible inner-model schema gives all ZF axioms internally and the canonical constructible well-order gives AC, hence L satisfies ZFC; the large-cardinal definition verifies that the same ordinal is uncountable, regular and strong limit there. Apply the formal inner-model clause fragment by fragment to obtain the stated consistency implication. No external well-order of the original universe is used.
items.axiom_base: ZF+DC in the source model; L satisfies ZFC plus an inaccessible cardinal

items.title: Exact equiconsistency of universal measurability and an inaccessible

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: ZFC plus an inaccessible cardinal and ZF+DC plus every set of reals Lebesgue measurable are equiconsistent. The same lower bound already follows from universal boldface Sigma^1_3 measurability under Countable Choice.
items.proof_plan: For the upper bound invoke the published, uniformly formalizable Solovay Levy-collapse construction from an inaccessible: its HOD(S) model satisfies ZF+DC and makes every real set measurable. For the lower bound invoke the preceding constructible-inner-model theorem. The forcing and inner-model compilers convert both semantic constructions to finite-fragment consistency proofs. Keep the inaccessible assumption on the Solovay branch and omit it entirely from the Baire-property branch; this separation is the point of the pair.
items.axiom_base: Metatheory of relative consistency; exact object theories are stated in both directions

items.title: Shelah's model separates universal Baire property from universal measurability

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
references.locator: Main Theorem 5.1 and Conclusions 5.1A and 7.17, pp. 18-19 and 43-44

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals
references.locator: Theorems 3.1-3.2 and discussion after Theorem 3.2, p. 43

items.statement: Relative to Con(ZFC), it is consistent that ZF+DC holds, every set of reals has the Baire property, and not every set of reals is Lebesgue measurable. Thus universal Baire property does not entail universal Lebesgue measurability over ZF+DC.
items.proof_plan: First pass inside the starting ZFC model M to L^M. If L^M has no inaccessible, use L^M; otherwise let κ be the least inaccessible of L^M and use the set model (L^M)_κ. In either case the chosen constructible ZFC model satisfies CH and its own constructible universe has no inaccessible. Perform the ccc Shelah construction over that model and take the repaired hereditary real-and-ordinal/HOD(S) inner model N. N has the same ordinals, reals and omega_1 as the ccc extension, and every real set in N has BP. Constructibility is absolute between these transitive same-ordinal models, so L^N has no inaccessible. If N made every real set measurable, the preceding L-only lower-bound theorem would make omega_1^N inaccessible in L^N, a contradiction. Formalize the two internal-L cases and ccc preservation fragment by fragment. The argument proves existence of a nonmeasurable set without selecting one.
items.axiom_base: Relative consistency over ZFC; the final inner model satisfies ZF+DC

title: Shelah's Baire-Property Model and Inner-Model Lower Bounds: Examples and Counterexamples

items.title: A universal-meagre stage absorbs an old nowhere-dense tree

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: Let S be an old perfect nowhere-dense binary tree and let (t,T) be a UM condition. There is a direct extension whose generic F-sigma code contains [S]. For the singleton closed nowhere-dense set {0^omega}, this extension can be displayed level by level.
items.proof_plan: Choose a level beyond t at which every node of T has a splitting extension. There are only finitely many S-sections at that level. Assign each one to a distinct section of an enlarged perfect nowhere-dense witness tree and record the required finite prefix substitutions; the extension forces [S] into the corresponding finite union of rearranged copies of [U_G]. For {0^omega}, one prefix substitution sends the zero branch into a chosen branch of U_G, while the reserved sibling verifies nowhere density. This displays one finite stage of the countable F-sigma envelope from the absorption lemma and does not claim that the generic tree itself directly contains every old tree.
items.axiom_base: ZF

items.title: Cylinder covers generate the Frechet tails in the Raisonnier filter

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: For fixed n, enumerate the finitely many length-n binary strings s and use their cylinders [s] as a countable cover of L[x]∩2^omega. Any two distinct reals in one cylinder first differ at a coordinate at least n. Hence omega minus n belongs to F(x), concretely demonstrating that F(x) extends the Frechet filter.
items.proof_plan: List all 2^n strings and pad the finite list by empty sets to an omega-sequence. Every binary real extends exactly one listed string. If u and v lie in the same cylinder they agree below n, so h(u,v)≥n; therefore the union of all H([s]) is contained in the cofinite tail of coordinates at least n. Apply the defining cover criterion. Check n=0 separately: the one empty-string cylinder gives omega itself.
items.axiom_base: ZF

items.title: Uniform null capture for a constant block function

references.title: Hiromi Ishii, Regularity Properties and Inaccessible Cardinals

items.statement: For the constant function f(n)=0, the uniform construction gives N_f as the intersection of the tail unions of the independent blocks B_(n,0). It is a null G-delta. Whenever an open U of measure below one contains N_f, the finite capture sets satisfy 0∈φ_U(n) for all sufficiently large n.
items.proof_plan: Write the first three tail unions and verify each is open. Their measures are bounded by the geometric tails sum_{n≥k}2^{-(n+1)}=2^{-k}, so the intersection is null. Apply the capture proof to K=2^omega minus U: find a basic cylinder [s] and tail index k missed by K; for all n beyond k and n(s), K∩[s]∩B_(n,0) is empty, so 0 lies in A_s(n) and hence φ_U(n). This illustrates the eventual, not pointwise, nature of capture.
items.axiom_base: ZF

items.title: False: the all-Baire-property model needs an inaccessible

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?

items.statement: False: obtaining a model of ZF+DC in which every set of reals has the Baire property requires the consistency of an inaccessible cardinal. In fact its consistency strength is exactly ZFC, whereas making every set of reals Lebesgue measurable has the consistency strength of an inaccessible cardinal.
items.proof_plan: The Baire-property equiconsistency theorem gives Con(ZFC) iff Con(ZF+DC+all BP), directly refuting the alleged inaccessible requirement. Contrast this with the exact measurability equiconsistency theorem. The separation theorem supplies a single relative model satisfying all BP but not all measurability, so the contrast is semantic as well as a comparison of upper bounds. Do not infer from the lower bound for measurability any lower bound for BP.
items.axiom_base: Metatheory of relative consistency

items.title: Amalgamating two sweet models over a common complete subalgebra

references.title: Saharon Shelah, Can You Take Solovay's Inaccessible Away?
references.locator: Claim 7.4 and Lemma 7.5, printed pp. 35-36; Claims 7.12-7.13 and Main Lemma 7.14, printed pp. 41-43

items.statement: Let (P_1, Q_1, E^1_n) and (P_2, Q_2, E^2_n) be sweetness models whose complete Boolean algebras share a common complete subalgebra B_0, with B_0 contained in BA(P_1) and in BA(P_2). Then the amalgam P_1 *_{B_0} P_2 is sweet: below any condition of the amalgam there is a single modulus k such that every n >= k and every two conditions in the same E_n-class are compatible, the canonical embeddings of P_1 and P_2 into the amalgam are complete, and BA(P_1 *_{B_0} P_2) inherits the countable chain condition from the omega-one sweet construction.
items.proof_plan: Instantiate the amalgamation theorem with the two sweet notions, taking Claim 7.4's uniform modulus as the single k that witnesses sweetness below an arbitrary condition, and Claim 7.12's E_n-classes to identify the conditions that are forced to be compatible. Lemma 7.5 then makes the amalgam sweet; Claim 7.13 extends the canonical isomorphism of the two complete subalgebras over B_0, and Main Lemma 7.14(a) supplies the countable chain condition together with the completeness of the embeddings. The example is the concrete witness the B companion asks for: two sweet models glued over one countably generated complete subalgebra, with the amalgamation verified rather than asserted.
items.axiom_base: ZF+DC through the amalgamation and isomorphism-extension suppliers; the ccc instance inherits ZFC+CH from the omega-one construction
